#### 1. chondrodysplasia-pseudohermaphroditism syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.452)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5358346)

**Proposed mechanism:** VCP (HGNC:12421) —DISRUPTS→ proteostasis (GO:0006996); proteostasis (GO:0006996) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal protein aggregate accumulation (HP:0003208); proteostasis (GO:0006996) —LEADS_TO→ Bone mineralization defect (HP:0005844); Abnormal protein aggregate accumulation (HP:0003208) —LEADS_TO→ Dementia (HP:0000715); Bone mineralization defect (HP:0005844) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322). Mutations in VCP (involved in protein quality control and degradation) lead to impaired proteostasis. This general cellular dysfunction results in abnormal protein aggregate accumulation (common to both diseases), and further manifests as specific phenotypes like dementia in IBD-FTD and bone and growth defects in CDPHS.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in VCP that are exclusively associated with one disease and not the other, or demonstration that the two diseases converge on completely independent molecular pathways downstream of VCP. _(variant: rs141004485 (VCP V374F) has a gnomAD allele frequency of 0.0002, consistent with a rare disease variant.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting VCP or downstream components of the proteostasis network could offer therapeutic strategies for both inclusion body myopathy with Paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia type 1 and chondrodysplasia-pseudohermaphroditism syndrome, particularly for managing protein aggregate accumulation.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of VCP and the proteasome degradation pathway in these distinct diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring protein homeostasis, potentially benefiting patients with both inclusion body myopathy with Paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia type 1, and neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, hypotonia, and absent language.
